c. Groundwater
Groundwater will not be affected by the project to any measurable degree. The absence of polluting factors, the limited degree of additional paved areas, and the limited amount of subsurface activity are factors that support the conclusion that neither the quality nor the availability of groundwater within the project, city or region will be impacted. Groundwater could interfere with redevelopment construction. Based on previous building experience in the general area of Fourth Street, groundwater has not been a problem. Again, individual building sites must be evaluated during the preliminary construction stage to determine if the water table will allow the type of structures proposed for redevelopment sites.
The Flood of 1972 did elevate the water table in the general area of the project, but since this situation will return to normal in time, there is no anticipated long range impact on the project from the excessive groundwater caused by the storm and flooding. There is a possible, but remote, situation that deals with a fluctuation of the water table acting on the project's underlying bedrock formations. An environmental impact statement prepared by the U. S. Army Corps of Engineers covering a proposed flood control project for South Harrisburg and vicinity, contains the following statement on this possibility.
"After the Flood of 1972, increased recharge to acquifers in carbonate rocks raised the elevation of the groundwater table above the surface creating short-lived ponds and lakes in local depressions until the ground water level subsided. Rapid prolonged fluctuations of the groundwater level in carbonate areas, especially in those rocks which are well jointed, can cause surface subsidence. This condition should be anticipated when ground water levels return to their normal levels.
No major problems have occurred or should occur in areas underlain by the Martinsburg Formation as a result of Storm Agnes flood waters except in very small areas which contain limestone or dolomite."
No incidences of subsidence in the project area, due to the above described conditions, have been reported since the flooding.
